doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Moving to Philadelphia and working with Clifford Jordan in 1976
summary: Ware follows his wife to Philadelphia, plays Detroit with Clifford Jordan and records "Remembering Me" for Muse.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: But you had come down here from Brooklyn to Philadelphia to live.
Yeah, uh-huh. I had to get away from -- had to follow you on down. You (inaudible). So I was following my wife, you know.
And how about living and working in

Well, to me, it's ideal, to get from Philly to New York. You know, this is kind of away from all that ratrace in New York and if you can gig, you can go up to New York and record, come on back home. Well, you know what's been happening now, I've been working with Clifford Jordan on and off, say, back in '76, before I really got ill. We played, Cliff and I, we worked Guadalupe, (unintelligible) club they had. No, first we went to Detroit for ten days. We had Roy Burrowes on trumpet, George (unintelligible) on drums, Clifford Jordan and myself. Pianoleess quartet. We worked ten days out there at the keystone -- no, the Keyboard Lounge.

And then we played a college out there, a concert. Come on back to Philly and he went on back up to New York and Clifford called me up, said, "We got a record date." We did a record date for Muse. Was just released this year. It's called "Remembering Me," with the same personnel except we had Chris Anderson, blind Chris Anderson, playing piano. We had some vocals on there. A young man named Hank Diamond Smith that put words to "Prayer to the People," one of Clifford's arrangements, and the Powerful Paul Robeson, another Clifford tune.
Incidentally, we had Clifford's daughter Donna singing and Thelonius Monk's daughter Boo-boo. Maybe you'll
get a chance to hear that one of these days. It's been out, like I said, a few months now.
